html:
A great temple to the god Amun at the foot of Jebel Barkal, a flat topped sandstone mountain beside the Nile in what is now northern Sudan. It was the religious heart of the kingdom of Kush.

Egyptian armies under Thutmose III reached this far south around 1450 BCE, during the Egyptian conquest of Kush. They saw in the mountain, with its tall pinnacle of rock on one side, a home of Amun, and they built a temple and the town of Napata at its base.

When Egyptian rule faded, the Kushites kept the cult and made it their own. Kings of Napata held that Amun of Jebel Barkal chose them and crowned them here. Piye enlarged the temple and set up his victory stela in it after conquering Egypt, and later kings such as Taharqa added more temples and carved the pinnacle.

The site stayed sacred for over a thousand years. Royal pyramids stand nearby. In 2003 Jebel Barkal and the other sites of the Napata region were made a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
sum: A great temple to the god Amun at the foot of Jebel Barkal, a flat topped sandstone mountain beside the Nile in what is now northern Sudan. It was the religious heart of the kingdom of Kush.
